analysis.title: GS Basics - Systematic Unwinds. Repricing AI Capital Costs. Cyber Incidents
key_insights: Rolling de-risking across long/short funds spilled into systematic strategies on 10/22. Losses were widespread across fundamental long/short, and particularly acute in TMT, Asian long/short, multi-strat and systematic strategies. Popular longs fell and popular shorts rose.
Unconstrained momentum is in its worst drawdown since the GFC, outside COVID. The author compares it to 2018 but says the unwind is considerably more extreme.
AI versus SPX ex-AI had its worst relative day since the DeepSeek moment on 10/22. The author says that day made the least sense of any in the selloff.

The author suggests the AI selloff may reflect a repricing of the cost of capital rather than weaker AI demand. The assumption of unlimited cheap capital for the buildout is being challenged. Funding options are cutting capex, delaying deployment or raising equity, and none supports equity prices.
Underlying AI demand is described as unchanged and robust. AI remains a sizeable share of portfolios relative to long-term history despite the reduction in risk.

A pile-up of cyber incidents (critical PHP exploits, a serious Java vulnerability, a Python supply chain compromise) may have contributed to the AI concerns. The author reads it as bullish for cybersecurity because AI is cutting the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface grows with token growth.

Crude is extending its breakout, with front contracts taking out recent highs as the geopolitical risk premium widens into the weekend. Outcomes are described as highly binary. A rapid, targeted engagement with no secondary infrastructure damage could trigger a sell-the-news unwind, while retaliatory disruption at key energy chokepoints would leave balances severely constrained. The author says a lot is already in the price.

Rates have diverged from oil: AI selling is helping bonds, as the market is synthetically cutting capex and growth expectations. If the energy situation resolves, the author questions how much more relief rates get. If AI stabilizes and growth expectations recover, rates could come under pressure again, which is not a supportive reflexivity for equities.

The index broke lower on heavyweights while dispersion underneath was extreme. Equal weight/RSP closed near the highs of the session at +68bps, popular longs were down mid-single digits and popular shorts were flat to higher.

Next week's major hyperscaler results are the key catalyst, especially how backlog converts to revenue, the pace of deployment and what is said about funding. The author still expects frontier model development to stay robust.
Korea held up better than expected on 10/23 after being down a lot at the open. The author had expected another mid-single-digit decline, and the absence of an air pocket is called encouraging.

The author says electricals, aerospace and transport have been sold indiscriminately, and that at current levels the market is pricing some pretty extreme outcomes. Investors are reluctant to add risk because of political events and energy concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Underlying AI demand hasn't really changed and remains robust, frontier model development remains strong, and further advances are expected in coming weeks.
tension_points.bear_case: The assumption of effectively unlimited cheap capital for the buildout is being challenged, and cutting capex, delaying deployment or equity funding are not supportive of equity prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's major hyperscaler results: how they translate backlog into revenue, the pace of deployment and what they say about funding.
